deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls resource lifecycle behavior during deletion. While it helps prevent accidental removal, it does not directly affect the resource's security configuration, access control, or compliance posture.

labels.description:
GCP labels for this Feature.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels provide metadata for organisation, ownership, and resource management. They do not directly change access controls, encryption, authentication, or network exposure.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The full, unique name of this Feature resource
name.rationale: The name uniquely identifies the resource and supports organisation and management, but it does not directly affect access control, encryption, authentication, or network exposure.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project ID determines the GCP project to which the resource belongs, impacting resource isolation and access control.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Config Management spec

Set this field to MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC to enable Config Sync auto-upgrades, and set this field to MANAGEMENT_MANUAL or MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED to disable Config Sync auto-upgrades. Possible values: ["MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED", "MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC", "MANAGEMENT_MANUAL"]
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Controls whether Config Sync receives automatic upgrades. Enabling automatic management helps ensure security patches and supported versions are applied consistently, reducing the risk of running outdated or vulnerable components.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Version of Config Sync installed
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the version of Config Sync to install, impacting the features and security posture of the deployment.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: ConfigSync configuration for the cluster

Enables the installation of ConfigSync. If set to true, ConfigSync resources will be created and the other ConfigSync fields will be applied if exist. If set to false, all other ConfigSync fields will be ignored, ConfigSync resources will be deleted. If omitted, ConfigSync resources will be managed depends on the presence of the git or oci field.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Controls whether Config Sync is enabled, directly affecting the deployment's configuration management capabilities and security posture.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The Email of the Google Cloud Service Account (GSA) used for exporting Config Sync metrics to Cloud Monitoring. The GSA should have the Monitoring Metric Writer(roles/monitoring.metricWriter) IAM role. The Kubernetes ServiceAccount 'default' in the namespace 'config-management-monitoring' should be bound to the GSA.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google Cloud service account used to export Config Sync metrics. Correct service account configuration helps enforce least-privilege access and ensures only authorized identities can write monitoring metrics.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Set to true to enable the Config Sync admission webhook to prevent drifts. If set to 'false', disables the Config Sync admission webhook and does not prevent drifts.
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Controls whether Config Sync prevents configuration drift through the admission webhook. Enabling drift prevention helps enforce approved configurations, reducing the risk of unauthorized or non-compliant changes.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Specifies whether the Config Sync Repo is in hierarchical or unstructured mode
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the repository structure used by Config Sync. This affects configuration organization and management but does not directly impact authentication, authorization, encryption, or the security posture of the deployed resources.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Git repo configuration for the cluster
The Google Cloud Service Account Email used for auth when secretType is gcpServiceAccount
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google Cloud Service Account used to authenticate to the Git repository. Correct service account configuration helps enforce secure authentication and least-privilege access to repository resources.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: URL for the HTTPS Proxy to be used when communicating with the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the HTTPS proxy used for communication with the Git repository. Correct proxy configuration helps ensure secure network routing, enforces organizational network policies, and reduces the risk of unauthorized traffic interception or bypass of security controls.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The path within the Git repository that represents the top level of the repo to sync
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: This Specifies the directory within the Git repository that Config Sync synchronizes. This affects configuration organization and repository structure but does not directly control authentication, authorization, encryption, or network security.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Type of secret configured for access to the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Determines the authentication method used to access the Git repository. Selecting an appropriate secret type helps ensure secure authentication and protects repository access from unauthorized use.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The branch of the repository to sync from. Default: master
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Git branch used as the source of synchronized configurations. Restricting synchronization to approved and protected branches helps prevent deployment of unauthorized, unreviewed, or non-compliant configurations.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The URL of the Git repository to use as the source of truth
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: This field defines the trusted source of configuration. If the repository URL is changed to an unauthorized repository, Config Sync could deploy malicious or unapproved configurations.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Git revision (tag or hash) to check out. Default HEAD
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Git revision (tag or commit hash) used as the source of synchronized configurations. Restricting synchronization to approved revisions helps prevent deployment of unauthorized, unreviewed, or insecure configuration changes.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Period in seconds between consecutive syncs. Default: 15
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: A shorter synchronization interval ensures approved security policies and configuration changes are enforced more quickly, minimizing the window during which outdated or non-compliant configurations remain active.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: OCI repo configuration for the cluster
The Google Cloud Service Account Email used for auth when secretType is gcpServiceAccount
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the Google Cloud Service Account used to authenticate to the OCI repository. Proper service account configuration helps enforce secure authentication and least-privilege access to configuration artifacts.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The absolute path of the directory that contains the local resources. Default: the root directory of the image
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the directory within the OCI image that contains the configuration resources to synchronize. This affects the organization and location of configuration files but does not directly impact authentication, authorization, encryption, or network security.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Type of secret configured for access to the Git repo
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Determines the type of secret used to authenticate when accessing the repository. Proper secret configuration helps ensure secure authentication and protects repository access from unauthorized use.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: The OCI image repository URL for the package to sync from
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifing the OCI repository used as the trusted source of synchronized configuration packages. Ensuring the repository URL points to an authorized and trusted source helps prevent synchronization of unauthorized or malicious configurations.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Period in seconds between consecutive syncs. Default: 15
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the interval between synchronization operations. Appropriate synchronization frequency helps ensure security and configuration updates are applied promptly, reducing configuration drift and the risk of outdated or non-compliant configurations.

fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.description: Version of Config Sync installed
fleet_default_member_config.configmanage.rationale: Specifies the installed version of Config Sync. Using supported and up-to-date versions helps ensure security patches, bug fixes, and protection against known vulnerabilities are applied.

fleet_default_member_config.mesh.managem.description: Whether to automatically manage Service Mesh Possible values: ["MANAGEMENT_UNSPECIFIED", "MANAGEMENT_AUTOMATIC", "MANAGEMENT_MANUAL"]
fleet_default_member_config.mesh.managem.rationale: Determines whether Service Mesh is managed automatically or manually. The selected management mode influences the timely application of security updates, maintenance, and the overall security posture of the Service Mesh deployment.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Policy Controller spec
Configures the version of Policy Controller
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Specifies the installed version of Policy Controller. Using supported and up-to-date versions helps ensure security patches, bug fixes, and protection against known vulnerabilities are applied while maintaining effective policy enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configuration of Policy Controller
Interval for Policy Controller Audit scans (in seconds). When set to 0, this disables audit functionality altogether.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls the frequency of Policy Controller audit scans. Appropriate audit intervals help detect policy violations promptly, while disabling or excessively delaying audits may allow insecure or non-compliant configurations to remain undetected.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The maximum number of audit violations to be stored in a constraint. If not set, the internal default of 20 will be used.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls the maximum number of policy violations retained for each constraint. Appropriate limits help maintain visibility into compliance issues and support effective security auditing and incident investigation.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The set of namespaces that are excluded from Policy Controller checks. Namespaces do not need to currently exist on the cluster.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Specifies namespaces that are excluded from Policy Controller enforcement. Exempting namespaces can bypass security and compliance checks, increasing the risk of unauthorized or non-compliant workloads.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configures the mode of the Policy Controller installation Possible values: ["INSTALL_SPEC_UNSPECIFIED", "INSTALL_SPEC_NOT_INSTALLED", "INSTALL_SPEC_ENABLED", "INSTALL_SPEC_SUSPENDED", "INSTALL_SPEC_DETACHED"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Determines the installation and operational state of Policy Controller. Disabling, suspending, or detaching Policy Controller can prevent security and compliance policies from being enforced, increasing the risk of unauthorized or non-compliant workloads.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Logs all denies and dry run failures.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls whether Policy Controller logs denied requests and dry-run policy violations. Enabling logging improves security monitoring, auditing, and incident investigation by providing visibility into policy enforcement events.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Enables the ability to mutate resources using Policy Controller.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls whether Policy Controller can automatically modify resources to enforce security and compliance policies. Enabling mutation helps ensure workloads conform to approved security requirements before deployment.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Enables the ability to use Constraint Templates that reference to objects other than the object currently being evaluated.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls whether Policy Controller can evaluate policies that reference related Kubernetes resources. Enabling referential rules supports more comprehensive security and compliance validation across multiple resources.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Map of deployment configs to deployments ("admission", "audit", "mutation").
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the Policy Controller deployment component associated with the configuration. This serves as a logical identifier and does not directly affect authentication, authorization, encryption, or policy enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod affinity configuration. Possible values: ["AFFINITY_UNSPECIFIED", "NO_AFFINITY", "ANTI_AFFINITY"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Configures pod scheduling preferences for Policy Controller components. This affects workload placement and availability but does not directly impact authentication, authorization, encryption, or policy enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod replica count.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Specifies the number of Policy Controller pod replicas. This influences service availability and scalability but does not directly affect authentication, authorization, encryption, or security policy enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Container resource requirements.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for use by the running container.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines the maximum CPU available to the Policy Controller container. Inadequate limits may throttle policy evaluation and reduce the reliability of security enforcement, while excessive allocation may affect overall cluster resource availability.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines the maximum memory available to the Policy Controller container. Insufficient memory limits may cause container termination and interrupt security policy auditing or enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Requests describes the amount of compute resources reserved for the container by the kube-scheduler.
CPU requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines the CPU requested for the Policy Controller container. Insufficient CPU allocation can cause performance degradation or delayed policy evaluation, potentially allowing non-compliant resources to remain undetected.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Memory requirement expressed in Kubernetes resource units.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines the memory requested for the Policy Controller container. Insufficient memory allocation can cause instability or service disruption, reducing the availability and reliability of policy enforcement.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Pod tolerations of node taints.
Matches a taint effect.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Determines which taint effect the Policy Controller pod can tolerate. An overly permissive or incorrect value could allow the pod to run on unsuitable or security-sensitive nodes, affecting workload isolation and availability.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint key (not necessarily unique).
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the node taint that the Policy Controller pod can tolerate. Incorrect configuration could permit scheduling on restricted nodes or prevent scheduling on intended nodes, affecting workload isolation and policy enforcement availability.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint operator.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines how the toleration matches a node taint, such as Equal or Exists. An overly permissive operator could allow the Policy Controller pod to run on restricted or unsuitable nodes, affecting workload isolation and security.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Matches a taint value.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Specifies the taint value that the Policy Controller pod can tolerate. An incorrect or overly broad value could allow scheduling on unintended nodes or prevent scheduling on approved nodes, affecting isolation and policy enforcement availability.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Monitoring specifies the configuration of monitoring Policy Controller.

Specifies the list of backends Policy Controller will export to. An empty list would effectively disable metrics export. Possible values: ["MONITORING_BACKEND_UNSPECIFIED", "PROMETHEUS", "CLOUD_MONITORING"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls where Policy Controller metrics are exported. Disabling monitoring or selecting an unsuitable backend could reduce visibility into policy violations, enforcement failures, and abnormal behaviour, delaying the detection and investigation of security issues.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Specifies the desired policy content on the cluster.
Configures which bundles to install and their corresponding install specs.
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Identifies the policy bundle installed on the cluster. Selecting an incorrect, unapproved, or insufficient bundle could result in required security controls not being enforced, increasing the risk of non-compliant resources being deployed.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: The set of namespaces to be exempted from the bundle.
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Defines namespaces that are excluded from the policy bundle. Exempting unnecessary or security-sensitive namespaces could allow workloads to bypass required policy controls; exemptions should therefore be limited to explicitly approved namespaces.

fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.description: Configures the installation of the Template Library.
Configures the manner in which the template library is installed on the cluster. Possible values: ["INSTALLATION_UNSPECIFIED", "NOT_INSTALLED", "ALL"]
fleet_default_member_config.policycontro.rationale: Controls whether the Policy Controller Template Library is installed on the cluster. Selecting NOT_INSTALLED or leaving the configuration unspecified could prevent required constraint templates from being available, reducing the coverage and effectiveness of security policy enforcement.

spec.description: Optional. Hub-wide Feature configuration. If this Feature does not support any Hub-wide configuration, this field may be unused.

spec.clusterupgrade.upstream_fleets.description: Specified if other fleet should be considered as a source of upgrades. Currently, at most one upstream fleet is allowed. The fleet name should be either fleet project number or id.
spec.clusterupgrade.upstream_fleets.rationale: Identifies the upstream fleet used as the source of cluster upgrades. Referencing an unauthorised or incorrect fleet could introduce unapproved upgrade configurations or versions, affecting cluster integrity, compatibility, and availability. Only explicitly trusted fleet project IDs or numbers should be allowed.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Post conditions to override for the specified upgrade.
Amount of time to "soak" after a rollout has been finished before marking it COMPLETE. Cannot exceed 30 days.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Defines the observation period after an upgrade rollout before it is marked complete. An insufficient soaking period may allow security, stability, or compatibility issues to go undetected, while an excessive period could delay subsequent critical upgrades. The duration should follow an organisation-approved range and must not exceed 30 days.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Name of the upgrade, e.g., "k8s_control_plane". It should be a valid upgrade name. It must not exceet 99 characters.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Identifies the cluster component whose upgrade configuration is overridden. An invalid or unauthorised upgrade name could apply the override to an unintended component or prevent required security upgrades. The value should be restricted to valid, organisation-approved upgrade names.

spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.description: Version of the upgrade, e.g., "1.22.1-gke.100". It should be a valid version. It must not exceet 99 characters.
spec.clusterupgrade.gke_upgrade_override.rationale: Specifies the target version for the cluster upgrade override. Selecting an outdated, unsupported, or unapproved version could expose the cluster to known vulnerabilities and compatibility issues. Only supported and organisation-approved versions should be permitted.

spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.description: Post conditions to override for the specified upgrade.

spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.soak.description: Amount of time to "soak" after a rollout has been finished before marking it COMPLETE. Cannot exceed 30 days.
spec.clusterupgrade.post_conditions.soak.rationale: Defines the observation period after a cluster upgrade rollout before it is marked complete. A period that is too short may allow security, stability, or compatibility problems to remain undetected, while an excessive period could delay subsequent critical upgrades. The duration should follow an organisation-approved range and must not exceed 30 days.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.description: Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled for the entire fleet. If UNSPECIFIED, fleet logging feature is disabled for the entire fleet.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.d.description: Specified if applying the default routing config to logs not specified in other configs.
Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled. Possible values: ["MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "COPY", "MOVE"]
spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.d.rationale: Controls how fleet logs are routed to the fleet host project. Selecting MODE_UNSPECIFIED disables fleet logging and may reduce visibility into security events. COPY or MOVE also affects log availability in source projects, so the mode should follow the organisation's approved logging and retention requirements.

spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.f.description: Specified if applying the routing config to all logs for all fleet scopes.
Specified if fleet logging feature is enabled. Possible values: ["MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "COPY", "MOVE"]
spec.fleetobservability.logging_config.f.rationale: Controls how logs from all fleet scopes are routed to the fleet host project. MODE_UNSPECIFIED can disable fleet-wide logging and reduce visibility into security events, while COPY or MOVE affects where logs remain available. The mode should comply with approved central logging and retention requirements.

spec.multiclusteringress.config_membersh.description: Fully-qualified Membership name which hosts the MultiClusterIngress CRD. Example: 'projects/foo-proj/locations/global/memberships/bar'
spec.multiclusteringress.config_membersh.rationale: Identifies the fleet membership that hosts the MultiClusterIngress configuration. Referencing an incorrect or unauthorised membership could direct ingress configuration through an unintended cluster, affecting traffic routing, exposure, availability, and administrative control. Only explicitly approved membership resource names should be permitted.

spec.rbacrolebindingactuation.allowed_cu.description: The list of allowed custom roles (ClusterRoles). If a custom role is not part of this list, it cannot be used in a fleet scope RBACRoleBinding. If a custom role in this list is in use, it cannot be removed from the list until the scope RBACRolebindings using it are deleted.
spec.rbacrolebindingactuation.allowed_cu.rationale: Controls which custom ClusterRoles can be assigned through fleet-scope RBAC role bindings. Allowing unapproved or overly privileged roles could grant excessive permissions and enable unauthorised access or changes across clusters. The list should be restricted to explicitly approved least-privilege roles.

spec.workloadidentity.scope_tenancy_pool.description: Pool to be used for Workload Identity. This pool in trust-domain mode is used with Fleet Tenancy, so that sameness can be enforced. ex: projects/example/locations/global/workloadidentitypools/custompool
spec.workloadidentity.scope_tenancy_pool.rationale: Identifies the Workload Identity Pool used as the fleet tenancy trust domain. Referencing an incorrect or unauthorised pool could allow workloads to assume unintended identities or access resources across trust boundaries. Only an explicitly approved Workload Identity Pool resource should be permitted.
